back: A dated, first-person record of events, thoughts and feelings.
Writing as a particular person, using their knowledge, feelings and voice.

front: Key feature of a good journal
back: Reflection: feelings, reasons and lessons, not just a list of events.
Short introduction → Name: words (new line per turn, no inverted commas) → closing thanks.
A question inviting a full answer (What…? How…? Why…?), not just yes or no.
Background → experience → views → future plans or advice.
Mostly past for the day's events; present for current feelings; will for plans.
Use its details from the character's viewpoint and develop feelings and reasons in your own words.
